wa_viper_head.blurb: Viper Head is a cliff in the Kettle Valley near Curlew in northeast Washington, picked out by a face whose shape suggests an open snake mouth. About ten routes mix gear climbs and bolted lines, with a few that run to two pitches. Grades run from 5.7 up to the low 5.10s, and the largest group sits around 5.10, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate trad and sport. The cliff is split into a lower face above a boulder field and a wider upper face reached by a diagonal scramble up and right.

wa_washout_the.blurb: The Washout is a small bouldering spot in Icicle Canyon near Leavenworth, created when a landslide in late 2011 swept down the canyon wall and left two big boulders, each about the size of a shed or garage, stranded in the debris. Local climbers cleaned them and found about ten problems. Difficulty is spread from V1 through the mid grades, with the bulk around V1 to V4 and a handful of harder lines up to V8. By the fall of 2013 the slide scar had greened up, with a stream and some trees giving shade. The ground here has shifted before, so conditions can differ from older descriptions.

wa_oz.blurb: Oz is a compact crag in the upper-left corner of the Cheeks at Index, the part of the Index town walls known for its steep, clean rock. It stands apart from the neighboring Black Sea section thanks to its mix of corners, splitters and aretes. The ten climbs here are mostly trad, with a couple of bolted lines and two aid routes, and the free climbs are demanding: grades begin around 5.11 and climb well into 5.12 and 5.14 territory. This is a place for experienced climbers rather than a first-day crag.

wa_woods_alcove_the.blurb: The Woods Alcove is a steep corner at Exit 32 near North Bend, tucked above the Woods crag and beneath the left end of World Wall. Reach it by following the base of the Woods routes uphill until the alcove appears. About ten routes are packed in, mostly bolted sport lines with a couple of trad climbs and one top-rope. Grades start around 5.10 and run into the low 5.13s, with most of the routes falling between 5.10 and 5.11, so it is better suited to solid intermediate climbers than beginners.

wa_the_towers.blurb: The Towers sit in the Planet Index section of the Index climbing area in the Skykomish Valley. The spot is half hidden by trees, but a few short towers poke up through the canopy at the top and give views. Expect many steep, fairly short cracks along with some aretes. Most of the ten routes are trad, and many can also be top-roped, plus one bolted line and one mixed route. Grades are mostly 5.7 to 5.10 with one harder 5.12, making it a decent choice for climbers working through the moderate crack grades.

wa_warrior_wall.blurb: Warrior Wall is a big dome in Icicle Canyon near Leavenworth, west of Peek-a-boo Tower, in an area of crags on the north side of the canyon that catch plenty of sun. A prominent left-facing dihedral marks its left side. The rock shows several colours, and almost all of the ten routes are trad, with a single bolted line. Grades start at 5.9 and spend most of their time in the 5.10s before reaching 5.11 and 5.12, with one sport route at 5.13. It is a wall for confident gear climbers.
